paperText: FICTIONAL REGRESSION PAPER: From Therapist Instructions to Exercise Software. Methods §3: We map the action and repetition count to an exercise template. The parser extracts arm side and repetitions from a controlled-language instruction. Example 2 / Figure 4: 'Raise the right arm five times' becomes 'for i in range(5): raise_right_arm()'. Changing the requested repetitions changes the loop bound while arm side selects the action function. The appendix releases three worked instruction/program pairs. Evaluation §5 compared generated programs with therapist-specified behavior, but patient records and the full proprietary generator are unavailable. This excerpt reports no numerical clinical improvement.

paperText: FICTIONAL REGRESSION PAPER: Thresholded Margin Classification. Methods §2: Method M computes z = 0.7*x1 + 0.3*x2 and predicts class 1 when z exceeds threshold tau. Baseline B predicts class 1 when x1 exceeds tau. Experiment §4 compares M with B on the released evaluation split using precision and recall. Condition C varies tau from 0.2 to 0.8; higher thresholds trade recall for precision on this split. Appendix A includes x1, x2 and true_label in evaluation.csv. No training or GPU is required for the released scoring rule. A study of other input distributions is proposed but not evaluated.

paperText: FICTIONAL REGRESSION PAPER: Normalized Fluorescence Dose Response. Methods §2: For each well, normalized response is (fluorescence - blank)/(untreated - blank). Figure 2 plots the median normalized response at each drug concentration. Experiment §3 repeats the measurements at 24 and 48 hours and compares the resulting curves. The authors release measurements.csv with concentration, time_hours, replicate, fluorescence, blank and untreated. Recreating the reported analysis requires only the released measurements, not a new wet-lab experiment. The paper does not test other compounds and does not claim a causal molecular mechanism.
